abstract.p: Nucleolus is disassembled when the nuclear envelope breaks down during mitosis prophase. However, the dynamics of nucleolus in meiotic prophase remain unclear. Here, by tracking nucleolar components of spermatocytes in mice, we show that the nucleolus is fragmented even before the breakdown of the nuclear envelope. Instead of dissolving in nucleoplasm or cytoplasm, the nucleolar components are reaggregated and fused with the XY body during prophase I of meiosis. The dynamic relocation of the nucleolar components to the XY body is governed by the ATR-dependent signaling pathway. Moreover, the relocated pre-ribosomal RNA (pre-rRNA) covers the entire X and Y chromosomes. The treatment with RNA polymerase I inhibitor BMH-21 only disrupts the accumulation of pre-rRNA but not other nucleolar components on the X and Y chromosomes. Surprisingly, this disruption of pre-rRNA induces the recruitment of RNA polymerase II to the XY body and partially abolishes meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI). Taken together, this study reveals pre-rRNA as a key epigenetic regulator for MSCI.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: The nucleolus is a nuclear membraneless organelle serving as the hub for ribosomal RNA (rRNA) transcription, processing, and ribosome assembly (Pederson, 1998; Ferrolino et al., 2018; Mitrea et al., 2016; Mitrea et al., 2018; Riback et al., 2020; Yao et al., 2019). Structurally, the nucleolus exhibits a tripartite architecture comprising the fibrillar center (FC), the dense fibrillar component (DFC), and the granular component (GC) (Yao et al., 2019; Feric et al., 2016; Boisvert et al., 2007). FC is the innermost layer where RNA polymerase I (Pol I) mediates 47 S pre-ribosomal RNA (pre-rRNA) transcription, which contains the sequences for mature 18 S, 5.8 S, and 28 S rRNAs, flanked by external transcribed spacers (5′-ETS and 3′-ETS) and separated by internal transcribed spacers (ITS1 and ITS2). DFC is the middle layer where the newly synthesized pre-rRNA is modified and processed. GC is the outer layer where the ribosomal protein subunits are integrated into rRNA to form the small and large ribosomal subunit precursors (pre-60S and pre-40S) (Barandun et al., 2018; Kater et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2021). These precursors are eventually shipped to cytoplasm to assemble mature ribosomes for protein translation.

The nucleolus continues generating pre-ribosomal particles during the interphase (Hori et al., 2023). However, during mitosis, the nucleolus is disassembled, and ribosomal biogenesis is halted. When the nuclear envelope breaks down during mitotic prophase, nucleolus is fragmented and dissolved (Leung et al., 2004; Roussel et al., 1996; Dundr et al., 2000). Early studies show that residual transcription machinery and pre-rRNA were kept at rDNA loci during mitosis, and nucleolus is reformed upon nuclear envelope assembly (Roussel et al., 1996). Recently, with advanced microscopy, we and others have revealed that nucleolar components, including pre-rRNA, cover condensed chromosomes during mitosis to avoid the clustering of the condensed chromosomes before segregation (Ma et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2025).

Different from mitosis, meiosis has an extended prophase I before the first round of cell division, especially for male germ cells (Griswold, 2016; de Rooij, 2001). The lateral element protein of the synaptonemal complex (SC), SYCP3, was used as a marker to identify the stages of spermatocytes (Yang and Wang, 2026). The prolonged prophase I in male germ cells can be further divided into five stages, namely leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis, during which homologous chromosomes are aligned together and associated with the SC (Chen et al., 2018; Lake and Hawley, 2021; Láscarez-Lagunas et al., 2020; Cesar and Kim, 2026). SPO11, a topoisomerase-like enzyme, generates DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) on homologous chromosomes to initiate meiotic recombination (Zheng et al., 2025; Paiano et al., 2020; Oger and Claeys Bouuaert, 2025; Zhang et al., 2020). These DSBs are ultimately repaired by homologous recombination repair machinery during meiotic prophase I (Lu and Yu, 2015; Brick et al., 2020; Dereli et al., 2024).

However, the male germ cells have two different sex chromosomes, the X and Y chromosomes. These two chromosomes share homology only at the pseudoautosomal region (PAR), thus forming synapses only in the PAR (Calderón et al., 2014; Kauppi et al., 2011; Raudsepp et al., 2012; Perry et al., 2001). Interestingly, these two sex chromosomes are conjugated together, forming the XY body, a membraneless nuclear body from pachytene to diplotene (Handel, 2004; Hoyer-Fender, 2003). While RNA polymerase II (Pol II)-mediated gene transcription is activated on autosomes during meiotic prophase I, gene transcription is silenced in the XY body, known as meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI) (Alavattam et al., 2021; Turner, 2007; Ichijima et al., 2012). Consistently, Pol II is specifically excluded from the XY body, although the underlying mechanism remains elusive (Namekawa et al., 2006). Moreover, due to lack of homologous templates, the repair of SPO11-mediated DSBs is prolonged in the XY body. Numerous DNA damage response factors are enriched in the XY body (Thacker et al., 2014; Kauppi et al., 2013). A typical example is the ATR-dependent phosphorylation of histone H2AX (aka γH2AX), also acting as the surrogate marker for the XY body (Saldivar et al., 2017; Widger et al., 2018; Royo et al., 2013; Ichijima et al., 2011; Lu et al., 2013).

In this study, we tracked the dynamic changes of the nucleolus in meiotic prophase I and found that the nucleolus was fused with the XY body. Pre-rRNA covers on the X and Y chromosomes and mediates MSCI.

sec.title: Nucleolus disassembles in the pre-leptotene spermatocytes
sec.p: To investigate the dynamic regulation of the nucleolus in meiotic prophase of male germ cells, we tracked the localization of pre-rRNA, the major component in the nucleolus (Pan et al., 2025). First, we examined the transition from the c-Kit-positive differentiating spermatogonia to pre-leptotene spermatocytes, which represents the transition from the final interphase to meiotic prophase I. Using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) (Gai et al., 2022), we observed that pre-rRNA clearly formed condensates in the c-Kit-positive differentiating spermatogonia and mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), suggesting that nucleoli are intact in the final interphase prior to meiosis (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1). However, in pre-leptotene, pre-rRNA became diffused in the nucleoplasm and was occasionally observed in discrete granules, suggesting that nucleoli start disassembly upon entry into pre-leptotene (Figure 1A).

sec.p: Since the nucleolus has three different layers, we examined the integrity of FC, DFC, and GC with different biomarkers, including POLR1E for FC, FBL for DFC, and NPM1 for GC (Pan et al., 2025; Lafontaine et al., 2021). Consistently, all three compartments exhibited widespread dispersion throughout the nucleoplasm in the pre-leptotene spermatocytes (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2). Of note, pre-rRNA and NPM1 diffused into a larger area (Figure 1A and B), indicating that pre-rRNA may largely associate with GC components during the nucleolar disassembly.

To further explore the nucleolus disassembly, we performed 5-ethynyl uridine (5-EU) incorporation assays. As 80–90% of nascent RNA is pre-rRNA, transient incorporation of 5-EU mainly labels pre-rRNA (Pan et al., 2025; Riback et al., 2023; Bao et al., 2018). As expected, 5-EU was incorporated into pre-rRNA in nucleoli of c-Kit-positive spermatogonia (Figure 1C). In sharp contrast, 5-EU incorporation into pre-rRNA was largely suppressed in pre-leptotene spermatocytes (Figure 1C). Meanwhile, RT-qPCR results showed that the 47 S transcript of pre-rRNA was largely reduced in prophase I spermatocytes compared to spermatogonia (Figure 1—figure supplement 3). These results suggest that Pol I-mediated pre-rRNA transcription is arrested when nucleoli start disassembly. Collectively, the nucleolus loses the tripartite architecture and the capability to synthesize pre-rRNA in the pre-leptotene spermatocytes (Figure 1D).

sec.title: Nucleolar components dynamically fuse with the XY body
sec.p: Next, we isolated spermatogenic cells from leptotene to diplotene using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) (Gaysinskaya et al., 2014; Zou et al., 2022), and analyzed the dynamic reorganization of nucleolar components in meiotic prophase I. At the leptotene stage, pre-rRNA and NPM1 appeared in many dispersed granules with different sizes, which began to aggregate as cells progressed into zygotene (Figure 2A and B). Upon entry into pachytene, coinciding with the formation of the XY body, we observed a striking spatial reorganization as both pre-rRNA and NPM1 were progressively recruited towards and subsequently sequestered in the XY body (Figure 2A and B). Quantitative analysis of signal intensity of pre-rRNA and NPM1 reveals a dynamic accumulation of both components in the XY body from early pachytene to diplotene (Figure 2A and B). By late pachytene, pre-rRNA and NPM1 were fully localized in the XY body (Figure 2A and B). Moreover, chromatin isolation by RNA purification (ChIRP)-seq analyses of pre-rRNA and CUT&Tag-seq analyses of NPM1 show that the enrichment of pre-rRNA and NPM1 was strictly confined to the X and Y chromosomes, but not on autosomes (Figure 2C). However, neither pre-rRNA nor NPM1 signals were observed in the vicinity of the sex chromosomes during leptonema or zygonema (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). In addition, other nucleolar components, such as POLR1E and FBL, showed similar dynamic relocation to the XY body during prophase I (Figure 2—figure supplement 2). Collectively, following nucleolar disassembly, the nucleolar components are reaggregated and fused into the XY body during meiotic prophase I (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).

sec.p: Moreover, different from nucleolar disassembly in mitotic prophase, the fusion of nucleolus and the XY body occurs when the nuclear envelope remains structurally intact throughout the pachytene stage (Figure 2—figure supplement 4). In addition, we examined and found that the rDNA loci remained spatially distinct and were not overlapped with the XY body (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), further confirming that nucleolus organizing regions are disassembled, and the nucleolar components are disassociated from the rDNA loci and fused with the XY body.

sec.title: ATR-mediated DNA damage response signaling drives the sequestration of nucleolar components to the XY body
sec.p: During meiotic prophase I, the delayed repair of programmed DSBs on the unsynapsed X and Y chromosomes triggers a localized DNA damage response, which is mediated by ATR-dependent γH2AX (Pacheco et al., 2018; Widger et al., 2018; Joshi et al., 2015; Kurzbauer et al., 2012; Carpenter, 1979), also acting as a surrogate marker of the XY body. Here, we examined whether the recruitment of nucleolar components to the XY body is dependent on DNA damage response. We isolated pachytene spermatocytes and treated them with the specific ATR inhibitor AZ20 for 24 hr to ablate DDR (Abe et al., 2022; Figure 3A). While γH2AX was abolished in response to the ATR inhibitor treatment, HR repair factors, including RAD51 and BRCA1 localized at the unsynapsed region of the X and Y chromosomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Interestingly, we found that along with the disruption of γH2AX, both pre-rRNA and NPM1 were absent from the XY body (Figure 3A and B). γH2AX started to be enriched at the unsynapsed region of the X and Y chromosomes 1 hr after the ATR inhibitor was washed away, and its localization in the XY body was fully recovered 4 hr after the treatment was removed. Following the recovery of the γH2AX signal, pre-rRNA and NPM1 were sequentially reaccumulated in the XY body (Figure 3A and B). In addition, pre-rRNA and NPM1 signals appear to be enriched within γH2AX-positive regions of the sex chromosomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). These results suggest that the fusion of nucleolar components with the XY body is dependent on the DNA damage response signals.

sec.p: It has been shown that genetically knocking out the H2ax gene abolishes the formation of the XY body as well as the synapsis between these two sex chromosomes. However, both RAD51 and BRCA1 remained on the elongated X chromosome in pachytene (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), suggesting that SPO11 still mediates DSBs on the X chromosome even in the absence of H2AX. Pre-rRNA and NPM1 were no longer localized to the X and Y chromosomes in H2AX-deficient spermatocytes (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 4). Thus, these results suggest that DSBs per se are not important for the recruitment of the nucleolar components to the XY body. Instead, it is the DNA damage response signals mediating the recruitment of the nucleolar components.

sec.title: Pre-rRNA mediates MSCI
sec.p: Since nucleolar components cover the transcriptionally silenced sex chromosomes, we wonder if nucleolar components may contribute to MSCI. To test this hypothesis, we treated isolated primary spermatocytes with Pol I inhibitor BMH-21 in vitro. BMH-21 recognizes GC-rich sequences not only to block Pol I binding to the promoter regions of rDNA but also to remove pre-rRNA from chromatin. Thus, BMH-21 treatment quickly released pre-rRNA from the XY body without affecting spermatocyte viability (Figure 4—figure supplements 1–3). However, the transient treatment did not affect the localization of NPM1 in the XY body (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), suggesting that rRNA species and nucleolar proteins may recognize different binding partners in the XY body. Moreover, exposure to 2.5 μM BMH-21 for 12 hr affected neither ATR nor γH2AX in the XY body (Figure 4—figure supplements 5–7), allowing us to assess the specific consequence of loss of pre-rRNA in transcription regulation on the sex chromosomes.

We then monitored transcriptional activity in the XY body using 5-EU labeling. In control pachytene spermatocytes, the XY body is devoid of nascent RNA because of MSCI (Figure 4A). Strikingly, upon exclusion of pre-rRNA from the XY body by BMH-21, we observed the accumulation of 5-EU-labeled nascent RNA species in the XY body, indicating a failure of MSCI (Figure 4A). To quantitatively examine the transcriptional reactivation, we isolated spermatocytes at the pachytene stage and treated the cells with BMH-21 (Figure 4B). We found that the overall gene expression on the X and Y chromosomes was significantly higher than that on autosomes (Figure 4B). Detailed transcriptomic profiling reveals that 237 X-linked genes and 9 Y-linked genes were significantly upregulated (≥ twofold change, Padj <0.05) (Figure 4C), confirming the specific transcriptional regulation by pre-rRNA. Moreover, we randomly selected representative X-linked genes (Pabir2, Dmd, Xlr, Ccnb3) and Y-linked genes (Uty, Usp9y, Zfy2), and performed gene-specific RT-qPCR to validate the RNA-sequencing results (Figure 4D).

sec.p: Because MSCI failure causes complete arrest and elimination of male germ cells at the pachytene stage of meiotic prophase I38, we next tested whether pre-rRNA inhibition could phenocopy this defect in vivo. To disrupt pre-rRNA localization within the XY body, BMH-21 was delivered to spermatocytes by rete testis microinjection in the 8-week-old male mouse (Figure 4—figure supplement 8). One week after injection, BMH-21-treated testes were markedly atrophic (Figure 4—figure supplement 9). The loss of PNA-positive round spermatids, which represent post-meiotic germ cells, indicated that BMH-21 treatment may cause defects at or before meiosis (Figure 4—figure supplements 10 and 11). The presence of only a few pachytene spermatocytes further suggested that spermatocytes might be eliminated at or after the pachytene stage (Figure 4—figure supplements 10 and 11). These results indicate that proper pre-rRNA localization within the XY body is required for meiosis.
Taken together, these results demonstrate that pre-rRNA is indispensable for maintaining MSCI in the XY body.

sec.title: Pre-rRNA mediates the exclusion of RNA Pol II from the XY body
sec.p: Under normal physiological conditions, the execution of MSCI requires the rigorous exclusion of RNA Pol II from the XY chromatin territory (Abe et al., 2022; Schier and Taatjes, 2020). Given the specific accumulation of pre-rRNA within this silent compartment, we hypothesized that pre-rRNA might play a role in restricting Pol II access. To test the hypothesis, we depleted pre-rRNA using BMH-21 and monitored Pol II localization. Strikingly, upon loss of pre-rRNA, we observed the relocation of Pol II in the XY body (Figure 5A). These results imply that the presence of pre-rRNA is essential to enforce the exclusion of Pol II from the sex chromosomes.

(D) Representative pre-rRNA ChIRP-seq and RNA Pol II CUT&Tag-seq profiles at X-linked loci.

sec.p: To substantiate the aforementioned spatial antagonism at the genomic level, we performed correlative ChIRP-seq (for pre-rRNA) and CUT&Tag (for Pol II) (Figure 5B). The sequencing data reveal a robust inverse correlation between pre-rRNA occupancy and Pol II binding. Specifically, BMH-21 treatment caused a marked reduction of pre-rRNA on the sex chromosomes, which was mirrored by a concomitant increase in Pol II occupancy across the XY chromatin (Figure 5B). Genome-wide peak analyses further confirm that pre-rRNA occupancy in the XY body coincides with the transcriptional suppression of Pol II targets (Figure 5C). Conversely, the depletion of pre-rRNA led to Pol II recruitment at specific loci of MSCI, such as Dmd, Ccnb3, and Zic3 (Figure 5D). Collectively, these results suggest that pre-rRNA functions as a critical spatial regulator that physically excludes Pol II from the XY chromatin, thereby maintaining the transcriptional silencing of the sex chromosomes in meiotic prophase.

sec.title: Pre-rRNA enforces a repressive chromatin state in the XY body
sec.p: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging as key architects of chromatin organization that modulate transcriptional outputs (Herman et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2018; Engreitz et al., 2013). Given the accumulation of pre-rRNA in the XY body, we asked whether the pre-rRNA regulates the accessibility of sex chromosomes to maintain MSCI. To verify this hypothesis, we assessed genome-wide chromatin accessibility changes upon pre-rRNA depletion. Pachytene spermatocytes were isolated and subjected to assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (ATAC-seq) (Figure 6A). Compared to the autosomes, the mean chromatin accessibility of the X chromosome (1.61-fold) and the Y chromosome (1.53-fold) was increased in response to the BMH-21 treatment (Figure 6A). The metagene and heatmap analyses demonstrate that BMH-21-induced expansion of open chromatin specifically across the sex chromosomes (Figure 6B and C). According to the peak calling, we found 1020 genes on the sex chromosomes that exhibited significantly gained accessibility (Figure 6D). To link this structural relaxation directly to pre-rRNA occupancy, we integrated these ATAC-seq data with our ChIRP-seq profiles. Notably, we found a high degree of overlap on 397 of these genes (84.47% of the analyzed subset) corresponding to genomic regions that lost pre-rRNA occupancy upon BMH-21 treatment (Figure 6E). Collectively, these results indicate that pre-rRNA limits chromatin accessibility of the XY chromatin, acting as a molecular barrier to maintain MSCI (Figure 6F).

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: In this study, we have shown that the nucleolus is disassembled in pre-leptotene. The nucleolar components are reaggregated in leptotene/zygotene and fuse with the XY body in pachytene/diplotene. This dynamic regulation of nucleolus is unique in meiotic prophase I. In mitosis prophase, nucleolus disassembly is associated with nuclear envelope breakdown. However, from pre-leptotene to diplotene, nuclear envelope is intact, suggesting that special signals associated with homologous chromosome packing and alignment may induce nucleolus disassembly in meiotic prophase I.

A more striking observation is that nucleolar components are reaggregated and fuse into the XY body. Like nucleolus, the XY body is a membraneless nuclear body (Alavattam et al., 2021). Here, we have shown that two different types of nuclear bodies fused together. Homogeneous fusion of liquid-liquid phase separation is commonly observed along with the increased level of condensate materials (Xue et al., 2025). However, heterogenous condensates fusion is rarely observed. Currently, the underlying mechanism driving the fusion of nucleolus and the XY body remains elusive. Nevertheless, we have shown that the fusion is dependent on the ATR-mediated signals, as ATR inhibitor treatment abolishes the retention of pre-rRNA and NPM1 in the XY body. Our earlier studies have shown that MDC1, a functional and binding partner of γH2AX in DNA damage response, recognizes pre-rRNA (Gai et al., 2022). It is likely that MDC1 targets pre-rRNA to the XY body. However, pre-rRNA can also be released by the treatment of BMH-21, a G/C rich sequence binder, suggesting that once pre-rRNA enters the XY body, it is associated with genomic DNA. Thus, it is possible that following the recruitment by MDC1, pre-rRNA expands onto the chromatin, which mimics the expansion of XIST on chromatin during the X chromosome inactivation.

In fact, similar to the role of XIST in transcription repression (Brockdorff et al., 1992; Hall and Lawrence, 2010; Zhang et al., 2025), pre-rRNA silences gene transcription in the XY body by repelling Pol II. Based on our observation, we propose that pre-rRNA physically occupies the XY chromatin and blocks the Pol II access to gene elements. Thus, pre-rRNA-mediated gene silencing may share the similar mechanism conducted by XIST during the X chromosome inactivation.

Pre-rRNA is the raw material to be processed into mature rRNA for ribosome assembly (Dörner et al., 2023). An important contextual consideration is whether ribosome biogenesis remains active during male meiotic prophase I. As shown in Figure S2, pre-rRNA transcript levels were extremely low in prophase I spermatocytes compared to Spg, indicating an arrest of rRNA synthesis upon meiotic entry. This temporal relationship raises the possibility that reduced engagement of nucleolar components in ribosome biogenesis may facilitate their redistribution and their participation in other biological processes. In addition, we show the evidence that pre-rRNA has been repurposed for gene silencing as non-coding RNA during meiotic prophase I. Moreover, our earlier study reveals that pre-rRNA may participate in HR repair for DSBs in the XY body (Gai et al., 2022). Thus, the collective evidence suggests the multiple roles of pre-rRNA during different biological processes.

In addition to pre-rRNA, other nucleolar components, including protein components, are also fused into the XY body. Such relocations are also mediated by the ATR-dependent signaling pathway. Like pre-rRNA, these protein components, such as NPM1, are also enriched on the chromatin. However, BMH-21 treatment did not release NPM1 from the XY body, suggesting that once NPM1 enters the XY body, it may recognize specific partners. The biological functions of these nucleolar proteins in the XY body need to be examined in the future. Of note, FBL, a methyltransferase catalyzing 2’-O-methylation on pre-rRNA (Yao et al., 2019), is specifically enriched on the unsynapsed axis of the X and Y chromosomes, where SPO11-mediated DSBs occur. However, POLR1E exhibited a diffuse distribution in the XY body. Thus, it is possible that these nucleolar proteins may be involved in meiosis-related events in the XY body, such as meiotic DSB repair. The differential localization pattern suggests that the nucleolar components may play distinct roles in the meiotic prophase I. We do not exclude the possibility that these nucleolar proteins also participate in MSCI.

In our study, we also noticed that loss of γH2AX in the XY body by the ATR inhibitor treatment does not abolish the structure of the XY body. However, the XY body cannot form in the H2ax gene knockout mice. It is possible that γH2AX mediates the priming of the XY body formation. Once the XY body is established, γH2AX is indispensable for the structural integrity of the XY body (Fernandez-Capetillo et al., 2003). Similarly, the γH2AX/MDC1 mediates the recruitment of pre-rRNA to the XY body. Once pre-rRNA gets into the XY body, it starts to expand onto the chromatin. However, we currently cannot exclude that the structural role other than the phosphorylation on Ser139 of H2AX is important for the XY body formation.

It is noteworthy that the nucleolus is reorganized into a nucleolus-like body in Drosophila spermatocytes. This structure serves as a platform for RNA Pol II-mediated transcription of Y-linked fertility genes (Fingerhut et al., 2026). In contrast, in mouse spermatocytes, nucleolar components, such as pre-rRNA and NPM1 are redistributed to the XY body. Their accumulation promotes Pol II exclusion and MSCI. The transcriptional outcomes differ between the two species: Y-linked genes remain transcriptionally active in Drosophila, whereas sex chromosomes are transcriptionally silenced in mice. These findings suggest that nucleolar organization has been evolutionarily adapted in a species-specific manner to meet distinct requirements for sex chromosome regulation during spermatogenesis.

In conclusion, this study delineates an unexpected link between the nucleolus and the XY body, two different nuclear bodies. We propose that the programmed disassembly of the nucleolus and the subsequent repurposing of pre-rRNA maintain the epigenetic silence of the X and Y chromosomes in meiotic prophase I.

sec.title: Mice
sec.p: All mice experiments were permitted by the Westlake University Animal Care and Use Committee and were performed according to the approved protocol. For all experiments, C57BL/6 J mice were used, except where otherwise specified. Wild-type mice were obtained from the Westlake University Animal Center. H2ax +/− mice were gifted by Linyu Lu (Zhejiang University). To generate gene knockout (KO) mice, heterozygous mating produces offspring. Spermatocytes were obtained from 3- to 4 week-old mice. All mice were housed in specific-pathogen-free conditions at ~22 °C with a humidity range of 40–70% and a 12 hr light/dark cycle.

sec.title: Collection and culture of spermatocytes
sec.p: Previously established methods for short-term culture were performed (Abe et al., 2022). Briefly, testes were collected from 3- to 4 week-old C57BL/6 J mice. Then the tunica albuginea was removed. The decapsulated testes were minced with a micro-dissecting scissor. They were transferred into 2 mL of Minimum Essential Medium alpha (Gibco, 12000–022) and incubated for 15 min at 35 °C with 1 mg/mL collagenase (type IV, Thermo Fisher) and 20 U DNase I (Vazyme, EN401). After that, the cells were centrifuged to discard the supernatant. The remaining seminiferous tubules were digested with TrypLE Express (Gibco, 12604021) with 50 U DNase I and 2 mg/mL collagenase IV for 10 min at 35 °C. The digestion was terminated by MEMα with 5% fetal bovine serum (FBS). The single-cell suspension was centrifuged at 500 g for 3 min and washed three times with MEMα. Cells were filtered into a 50 mL tube through a 40 μm cell strainer (Falcon, 352340). The cells were collected and cultured in MEMα.

For drug treatment experiments, the collected cells were cultured in MEMα containing DMSO (control), BMH-21 (Selleck, S7718), or AZ20 (Selleck, S7050). For recovery experiments, the control and treated cells were washed three times and collected by centrifugation at 500 g for 3 min after drug incubation. For ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage in meiosis, cells were treated with 10 Gy of X-ray. After 4 hr of recovery, the cells were collected for the next experiments.

sec.title: Meiotic chromosome spreads
sec.p: Meiotic chromosome spread slides were prepared as previously described (Alavattam et al., 2018). Some details and conditions were modified. For the fresh tissue, testes were excised from mice. The tunica albuginea was removed. The seminiferous tubules were placed in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Each testis was transferred to 1 mL PBS and gently unraveled with tweezers. Then, the seminiferous tubules were transferred to a hypotonic extraction buffer (30 mM Tris-HCl, 50 mM sucrose, 17 mM sodium citrate, 5 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM dithiothreitol, and 0.1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride) for further processing. After incubation on ice for 10 min, the same volume of sucrose (100 mM) was added to the hypotonic extraction buffer. Seminiferous tubules were mashed with tweezers and pipetted up and down several times. The suspension was filtered through a 70 μm cell strainer (Corning, 431751). After that, the slides were soaked in fixation buffer (1% paraformaldehyde [PFA], 0.1% Triton X-100, pH 8.2) for several minutes. Take the slides out and keep them flat. The 100 μL suspension was added to the slides. A slight movement spreads the suspension and fixation buffer over the entire slide. The slides were placed in humidified chambers at room temperature and air-dried overnight. The meiotic chromosome spread slides were stored in slide boxes at −80 °C.

sec.title: Immunofluorescence and RNA FISH
sec.p: The chromosome spread slides were washed three times in PBS. Then, cells were blocked for 30 min at room temperature in PBS containing 3% bovine serum albumin (BSA). After that, cells were incubated with 200 μL dilution of primary antibodies in 1% BSA at 4℃ overnight. The slides were washed three times in PBS with 0.1% Tween 20 and then incubated for 2 hr with secondary antibodies at room temperature. After washing three times, DNA was counterstained with DAPI.

For FISH, slides were prepared as described previously (Namekawa, 2014). Cells were washed in PBS and dehydrated using 70, 80, and then 100% ethanol for 2 min each, followed by air-drying until completely dry. Then, cells were first incubated with wash buffer I (SMF-WA1-60, BioResearch Technologies) for 10 min at room temperature. The RNA probes were diluted with hybridization buffer (SMF-HB1-10, Bioresearch Technologies). The chromosome spreads were incubated with diluted probe solution, gently covered with Parafilm. The slides were put in a humidified chamber at 37 °C overnight. The next day, Parafilm was removed, and slides were incubated with the same wash buffer I for 20 min at room temperature. The slides were washed with PBS and counterstained with DAPI. The pre-rRNA probes were used in the previous study (Gai et al., 2022).
For RNA FISH and combined immunofluorescence (IF) experiments, the slides were fixed with 4% PFA after the secondary antibody incubation. Then, FISH was performed as described.
All of the images were obtained with a Zeiss LSM900 confocal microscope equipped with a 63 x/1.4 oil lens (Zeiss), and were processed using ImageJ.

sec.title: FACS
sec.p: Sub-populations of spermatogenic cells and spermatocytes were isolated from mice following a published protocol (Gaysinskaya et al., 2014; Zou et al., 2022). Briefly, the testicular cell suspensions were prepared as described above. The cells were resuspended in 2 mL of PBS containing 5% FBS and filtered through a 40 μm cell strainer (Corning, 352340). The filtrate was counted and diluted to 1×107 /mL cells. Then, add Hoechst 33342 (Invitrogen, H3570) at a final concentration of 10 μg/mL and incubate at 32 °C for 30 min. The cell suspensions were mixed every 5 min and kept in the dark to avoid light exposure. After that, the cell suspensions were washed with PBS containing 5% FBS and resuspended in 1 mL PBS containing 5% FBS and 2 μg/mL propidium iodide (Invitrogen, P3566, PI) for 10 min. Wash cells in 5 mL PBS containing 5% FBS three times, then centrifuge at 500 g for 3 min. Cells were sorted by BD FACSAria Fusion. The gating parameters are referred to the published method and modified according to the actual conditions (Zou et al., 2022). The sub-populations of spermatogenic cells were collected into 5 mL flow tubes containing 2 mL PBS with 5% FBS. The purity of sorting cells was confirmed by IF with the antibody against SYCP3.

sec.title: Detect the newly transcribed RNA in spermatocytes
sec.p: Spermatocytes were collected and cultured in a 6-well culture plate. Add 5-ethynyl-uridine (5-EU) to the culture medium at a final concentration of 1 mM for 2 hr. We also added DMSO as a negative control. After labeling cells with 5-EU, cells were collected and resuspended in PBS, centrifuged at 500 g for 3 min. Cells were fixed with fixation buffer (1% PFA, 0.1% Triton X-100, pH 8.2) on the cover glass. The cover glass was placed in humidified chambers at room temperature and air-dried overnight. IF was performed to detect γH2AX as described above. Next, to detect the newly transcribed RNA, we prepared the 500 μL click additive buffer (430 μL click reaction buffer, 20 μL CuSO4, 1 μL Azide 488, 50 μL click additive, Beyotime, R0301S) for each reaction. The cover glass with cells was placed in a 6-well culture plate and incubated with the click additive buffer for 30 min. Then, the click additive buffer was removed. Cells were washed three times with 1 mL PBS containing 3% BSA. DAPI was added, and the cover slip was placed on the glass slide.

sec.title: RNA extraction and RT-qPCR
sec.p: Cells were lysed in TRIzol (Invitrogen, 15596018CN) and RNA was extracted according to the standard protocol. Briefly, after different treatments, cells were collected into 1.5 mL tubes (Axygen, MCT-150-C). RNAs were washed with 75% ethanol. For each sample, the extracted RNA was dissolved in 20 μL DEPC water. In order to detect the specific gene expression, we synthesized cDNA with Hifair AdvanceFast 1st Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit (Yeason, 11149ES60). The products were diluted, and Hieff SYBR Green Master Mix (YEASEN, 11201ES03) was used for qPCR on SIA-PCR007 (Bio-Rad CFX Connect). Primers were designed according to the coding sequences from NCBI using Primer-BLAST and referenced to the data from PrimerBank. Cycle threshold values were recorded for the analysis. Data were from three technical replicates per sample. Significant differences were identified using Student’s t-tests.

sec.title: CUT&Tag assay and analysis
sec.p: The 1×104 spermatocytes were collected for the CUT&Tag assay (Vazyme, TD904) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, spermatocytes were resuspended in the wash buffer and the nuclei were collected. Then, the nuclei were incubated with ConA Beads for 10 min. The samples were incubated with the primary antibody and the secondary antibody. pA/G-Tnp transposase was used to cut the genome, and the DNA was extracted and subjected to PCR amplification to build a library. The sequencing process was commissioned by Nanjing Jiangbei New Area Biopharmaceutical Public Service Platform. Following sequencing, raw paired-end reads were subjected to a standardized bioinformatics pipeline for downstream analysis. Initial quality control and adapter trimming were performed to remove low-quality bases. The clean reads were then aligned to the mouse reference genome (mm10) using Bowtie2 (2.3.5.1). Peak calling was conducted with a q-value threshold of 0.05 and different peak analyses with a fold change of RPM ≥2. Alignment files (.bam) were loaded into the Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV).

sec.title: ChIRP
sec.p: ChIRP was carried out as previously described with a few modifications (Sallam et al., 2018). The pre-rRNA antisense oligo probes with 3′-Biotin-TEG modifications were designed by ChIRP Probe Designer. Optimize the sonication time (high setting, 30 s ON and 30 s OFF, 10 cycles). ChIRP probes were incubated with sonicated chromatin at 37 °C for 12 hr with rotation in a molecular hybridization apparatus. The purified DNA was sent to Nanjing Jiangbei New Area Biopharmaceutical Public Service Platform for library preparation and subsequent Illumina HiSeq sequencing.

sec.title: ATAC-seq
sec.p: Spermatocytes were isolated and treated for 12 hr with or without BMH-21. Then, pachytene spermatocytes were sorted as described above and lysed in 50 μL lysis buffer (ATAC-seq kit, Vazyme, TD711). Using two replicates per condition, libraries were prepared using the Hyperactive ATAC-Seq Library Prep Kit for Illumina (Vazyme, TD711) as described with slight modifications (Wu et al., 2025). DNA was amplified for 14 cycles and then purified using DNA Clean Beads, followed by elution with 22 μL of nuclease-free water. Finally, the libraries were sent to Nanjing Jiangbei New Area Biopharmaceutical Public Service Platform for sequencing.

sec.title: In vivo rete testis microinjection of BMH-21
sec.p: Mice were anesthetized by intraperitoneal administration of Avertin (250 mg kg⁻¹) and positioned supine. Following aseptic preparation, a single incision (~1.5 cm) was made above the genital area, and the testes were exteriorized by gently tractioning the fat pad. BMH-21 (10 μL, 50 μM) or DMSO was injected into the rete testis using a glass capillary under a stereomicroscope. At 1 week post-injection, testes were harvested and fixed in 4% PFA for further analysis.

sec.title: Quantification and statistical analysis
sec.p: The areas of different proteins and pre-rRNA were quantified with ImageJ. To quantify pre-rRNA or Pol II enrichment at the XY body, the XY body region was defined as the region of interest (ROI) based on SYCP3 staining and DAPI-dense chromatin. The signal area within this ROI was measured using ImageJ, and the occupancy rate was calculated as: (signal area within XY body)/(total XY body area)×100%. This value reflects the proportion of the XY body territory occupied by pre-rRNA or Pol II signals. These quantifications are based on the Analyze module. The main object of observation was selected using the rectangle tool. Data were collected and analyzed using GraphPad Prism 8. The relative fluorescence intensity data were obtained using ZEN 3.3. An unpaired Student’s t-test was used to determine statistical significance, defined as p<0.05.

body.p: This fundamental paper describes the role of the Pre-rRNA in meiotic sex chromosome inactivation in mouse spermatocytes. The cytological and genome-wide analyses on components of the nucleolus and chemical inhibition of RNA polymerase I for rDNA transcription provided solid evidence to support the authors' conclusion. The results shown in the paper are of interest to researchers in meiotic chromosome structure and the nucleolus.

The authors show that during prophase I of male meiosis, nucleoli disassemble and nucleolar components relocalize to the sex chromosome (XY) body. They further demonstrate that this process is regulated by the ATR-dependent signaling pathway that mediates meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI). Pharmacological disruption of pre-rRNA synthesis using the RNA polymerase I inhibitor BMH-21 leads to the recruitment of RNA polymerase II to the sex chromosomes and ectopic expression of sex chromosome-linked genes. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized role for pre-rRNAs in maintaining transcriptional silencing during meiosis. The study employs a combination of cell biology, genetics, and genomics approaches, and the conclusions are supported by compelling, well-organized data.

body.p: The following is the authors’ response to the original reviews.

disp-quote.p: Comments:

(1) The current study focuses on transcriptional regulation of the sex chromosomes. It would be interesting to know whether perturbation of pre-rRNA synthesis also affects transcription of autosomal genes.

body.p: Our RNA-seq analysis shows that BHM-21 treatment markedly affected the transcription of X- and Y-linked genes, with no obvious influence on the transcription of autosomal genes in pachytene spermatocytes (Figure 4B).

disp-quote.p: (2) Is ribosome biogenesis still active during prophase I of male meiosis? Additional discussion of the timing and extent of rRNA synthesis at this stage would help place the findings in a broader biological context.

body.p: To determine whether ribosome biogenesis remains active during meiotic prophase I, we examined 47S pre-rRNA levels by qPCR in spermatogonia (Spg) and prophase I spermatocytes. As shown in Figure S2, pre-rRNA transcript levels were extremely low in prophase I spermatocytes compared to Spg, indicating an arrest of rRNA synthesis upon meiotic entry. Notably, we observed prominent redistribution of nucleolar components to the XY body during prophase I. These findings suggest that reduced engagement of nucleolar components in rRNA biogenesis may facilitate their redistribution and their participation in other biological processes. We have added this discussion to the revised manuscript (Lines 283-289).

disp-quote.p: (3) A recent preprint reports active RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription of Y chromosome genes within nucleolus-like bodies (NLBs) during prophase I of meiosis in Drosophila male germ cells (https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.20.726666). These findings suggest that the meiotic nucleolus may have species-specific roles in regulating sex chromosome gene expression. It would be valuable for the authors to discuss how their findings compare with these observations and the potential evolutionary implications.

body.p: In Drosophila spermatocytes, the nucleolus is reorganized into a nucleolus-like body (NLB). This structure serves as a platform for RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription of Y-linked fertility genes. In contrast, in mouse spermatocytes, nucleolar components such as pre-rRNA and NPM1 are redistributed to the XY body. Their accumulation promotes Pol II exclusion and meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI). The transcriptional outcomes differ between the two species: Y-linked genes remain transcriptionally active in Drosophila, whereas sex chromosomes are transcriptionally silenced in the mouse. These findings suggest that nucleolar organization has been evolutionarily adapted in a species-specific manner to meet distinct requirements for sex chromosome regulation during spermatogenesis. We have discussed this point in the revised manuscript (Lines 317-326).

disp-quote.p: Summary:

The authors showed the localization pattern of nucleolus components, including Pre-rRNA, a precursor of rRNAs, changes during meiotic prophase I, particularly with the localization of these nucleolar components to the X-Y body, which shows inactivation of RNA polymerase II transcription, during pachynema. The localization of Pre-rRNA depends on ATR kinase and gammaH2AX. The chemical inhibition of rRNA transcription disrupts the binding of pre-rRNA to the X-Y body and suppresses the inhibition of the RNA polymerase II-mediated transcription on the sex chromosomes.
Strengths:

The cytological analysis, combined with the chemical inhibition, provided solid evidence to support the idea that, together with the remodeling of the nucleolus structure, pre-rRNA is an essential component of sex chromosome inactivation in male mouse meiosis. The role of pre-rRNA in sex chromosome inactivation in male meiosis helps our understanding of how the X-Y body, which would be a biological condensate, would be formed; e.g. for example, this Pre-rRNA may promote phase separation.
Weaknesses:

However, there is limited information on how Pre-rRNA is recruited to only sex chromosomes and how the RNA promotes the inactivation of sex chromosomes. Of course, these will be a target of future study. One major weakness of this paper is a poor description of the results, with fair presentation and interpretation of the data.

body.p: Following the reviewers suggestions, we have modified the manuscript. As listedbelow, we have addressed all the concerns raised by the reviewers point by point.

disp-quote.p: Major points:

(1) The authors studied the localization of pre-rRNA, which is the center of this study. However, the general structure of this RNA was poorly described in the text. For example, how this pre-rRNA is different from mature rRNAs. Importantly, how the authors detected pre-rRNA, not other rRNA species, should be described in the Figure and the text.

body.p: The primary pre-rRNA transcript contains the sequences that give rise to the mature rRNAs, together with the external transcribed spacers (5′-ETS and 3′-ETS) and internal transcribed spacers (ITS1 and ITS2). During rRNA maturation, these spacer regions are progressively removed through a series of processing steps and are therefore absent from mature rRNAs (PMID: 22342225). To specifically detect pre-rRNA, we performed RNA-FISH using probes targeting the ITS1 and ITS2 regions as described in the Methods section (Line 380-398). This probe design strategy has been reported in our previous study and cited in the Methods section (PMID: 34980897). Following your suggestion, we have now added a brief description of the general structural features of pre-rRNA and its distinction from mature rRNAs in the Introduction (Lines 36-39).

disp-quote.p: (2) For the dynamics of the localization of pre-RNA and/or NMP1 during the meiotic prophase I, it is very important to check the localization of these components in zygonema (or leptonema) by ChIP-seq (Figure 2C) to address whether these signals bind to the sex chromosome prior to pachynema.

body.p: As suggested, we performed additional ChIRP-seq and CUT&Tag-seq to detect the localization of pre-rRNA and NPM1 in leptotene/zygotene spermatocytes (GSE346625, GSE346622). The results indicate that neither pre-rRNA nor NPM1 associates with sex chromosomes at the leptonema-zygonema stage prior to pachynema (Revised Figure S3).

disp-quote.p: (3) For Pre-rRNA ChIP, how did the author IP the RNA? Do they have specific antibodies against the RNA? Please explain this in the text.

body.p: The pre-rRNA-associated chromatin was not isolated using an RNA-specific antibody. Instead, we employed Chromatin Isolation by RNA Purification (ChIRP), a well-established method for mapping RNA–chromatin interactions (PMID: 24457971). In this assay, biotinylated antisense DNA oligonucleotides complementary to pre-rRNA sequences were used to specifically capture pre-rRNA together with its associated chromatin, followed by streptavidin-based purification. The experimental procedure has been described in the Methods section (Lines 467-475).

disp-quote.p: (4) For Pre-rRNA ChIP-seq and CUT&Tag-seq (Fig. 2C, 3C), the signals are enriched in specific genomic regions. Please show where they are and discuss them.

body.p: Pre-rRNA/NPM1 signals appear to be enriched within γH2AX-positive regions of the sex chromosomes (Figure S8). This spatial overlap is consistent with our finding that ATR-mediated DNA damage response signaling drives the sequestration of nucleolar components to the XY body. Supporting this interpretation, inhibition of ATR or loss of H2AX markedly reduced the enrichment of both pre-rRNA and NPM1 on the sex chromosomes. We have discussed this point in the revised manuscript (Lines 155-158).

disp-quote.p: (5) In Figure S2, the staining patterns of PLRE1 and FBL are different; FBL seems to bind to chromosome axes, which should be mentioned in the text and, if possible, discussed in terms of the differential localization of nucleolar components on the X-Y body.

body.p: FBL was specifically enriched on the unsynapsed axis of the X and Y chromosomes, where SPO11-mediated DSBs occur. However, POLR1E exhibited a diffuse distribution in the XY body. Thus, it is possible that these nucleolar proteins may be involved in meiosis-related events in the XY body, such as meiotic DSB repair. The differential localization pattern suggests that the nucleolar components may play distinct roles in the meiotic prophase I. We have included the description and discussion of this part in the revised manuscript (Lines 302-306).

disp-quote.p: (6) Graphs in Figure 3 showed the order of the binding after ATRi washing: gammaH2AX>NPM1>Pre-rRNA. This kinetic difference is confirmed and should be mentioned in the text (and discussed).

body.p: We agree that the distinct recovery kinetics of γH2AX, NPM1, and pre-rRNA upon ATRi washout support a hierarchical recruitment model. After ATRi washout, γH2AX signals reappeared most rapidly, followed by the gradual re-accumulation of NPM1 and pre-rRNA. This distinct kinetics suggests that ATR-dependent γH2AX signaling precedes the recruitment of NPM1 and pre-rRNA. We have included related information in the revised manuscript (Lines 155-158).

disp-quote.p: (7) Figure 3C: It is clear that the absence of pre-rRNA and NMP1 in the gammaH2AX KO testis. It is important to show the localization patterns of these components in pachytene KO cells; e.g., no change in the localization.

body.p: As suggested, we performed additional IF-FISH analysis in wild-type and H2AX-knockout pachytene spermatocytes to examine the subcellular localization of pre-rRNA and NPM1. Both pre-rRNA and NPM1 were prominently enriched at the XY body in wild-type pachytene spermatocytes. In contrast, this XY body-associated enrichment was lost in H2AX-knockout pachytene spermatocytes. Notably, pre-rRNA remained colocalized with NPM1 in H2AX-knockout cells. These observations suggest that H2AX is required for the recruitment of pre-rRNA/NPM1 to the XY body, but is not required for their spatial association. These new data have been included in Figure S9 and described in the revised manuscript (Lines 164-166).

disp-quote.p: (8) EU incorporation experiment in Figure 4: Signals of EU in this figure are different from those in Figure1 C. This suggests the distinct loci for rRNA production between leptonema and pachynema. Please explain more. More importantly, it is very important to show the amounts and production rates of ribosomes or rRNAs during distinct stages of prophase I.

body.p: 5-EU (5-ethynyl uridine) is a nucleoside analog that is incorporated into all newly synthesized RNA, including both rRNA and mRNA, during active transcription. Therefore, the 5-EU signals we observed reflect the global transcriptional activity of all RNA polymerases (Pol I, Pol II, and Pol III), rather than rRNA production specifically. In pachytene spermatocytes, the XY body undergoes meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI), a process in which transcription on the sex chromosomes is largely silenced. However, Pol II-mediated transcription is robustly active on the autosomes during this stage. Therefore, the 5-EU signals we detected in pachytene cells predominantly originate from active Pol II transcription on autosomes, while the XY body remains largely devoid of 5-EU incorporation due to MSCI.

Following the reviewer’s suggestion, we further quantified pre-rRNA transcript levels at different stages of meiotic prophase I using quantitative RT-qPCR. Pre-rRNA transcript levels were extremely low in prophase I spermatocytes compared to Spg, indicating an arrest of rRNA synthesis upon meiotic entry (Revised Figure S2). These findings suggest that reduced engagement of nucleolar components in rRNA biogenesis may facilitate their redistribution and their participation in other biological processes. We have discussed this point in the revised manuscript (Lines 283-289).

disp-quote.p: (9) It is very important to show the localization of X-Y body markers such as Brca1, ATR, etc., in spermatocytes treated with BMH-21 to know which process is prevented with this inhibitor.

body.p: As suggested, we examined the localization of ATR and BRCA1 in pachytene spermatocytes following BMH-21 treatment. ATR localization to the XY body was unaffected by BMH-21 treatment. Together with our finding that ATR inhibition disrupts pre-rRNA accumulation at the XY body, these observations support the notion that ATR signaling is required upstream of pre-rRNA recruitment. In contrast, BRCA1 enrichment at the XY body was reduced by BMH-21, suggesting that BRCA1 accumulation at the XY body is potentially regulated by pre-rRNA. We have included these data in Figure S11C and S11D and added the corresponding description in the revised manuscript (Lines 180-181).

disp-quote.p: (10) Figure 4A clearly shows the localization of pre-rRNA in the X-Y body depends on active PolI transcription. Where is pre-rRNAs, which resided in the X-Y body after the treatment? Spreading to the nucleoplasm or degradation. Is it very important to analyze the amounts of rRNA species, including pre-rRNAs, under these conditions (and also during normal prophase I)?

body.p: As shown in Figure 4A, the prominent enrichment of pre-rRNA at the XY body was lost upon BMH-21 treatment. Instead, the residual pre-rRNAs were dispersed in the nucleoplasm. We also observed that BMH-21 treatment markedly reduced total pre-rRNA levels in pachytene spermatocytes (Author response image 1). Therefore, these results indicate that BMH-21 disrupts the enrichment of pre-rRNA at the XY body and reduces overall pre-rRNA abundance.

caption.title: BMH-21 reduces pre-rRNA levels in pachytene spermatocytes.
caption.p: RT-qPCR analysis of pre-rRNA in pachytene spermatocytes treated with BMH-21 (2.5 μM, 12 hours). Data are presented as mean ± SEM (n=3 biological replicates).

disp-quote.p: (11) The authors need to study the localization of nucleolar components including Pre-rRNA, in female meiosis.

body.p: We agree that examining the localization and dynamics of nucleolar components during female meiosis would be of considerable interest. However, the present study focuses specifically on the redistribution of nucleolar components to the XY body during male meiotic prophase I. The XY body is a male-specific chromatin domain formed by the largely unsynapsed X and Y chromosomes and is closely associated with meiotic sex chromosome inactivation and the ATR-dependent DNA damage response. Because female meiotic cells lack an equivalent XY body structure, investigating nucleolar organization during female meiosis would address a distinct biological question that is beyond the scope of the present study.

disp-quote.p: Minor points:
(12) Line 61-62, subtelomeric region: "pseudo-autosomal region" is better.

body.p: We have replaced "subtelomeric region" with "pseudoautosomal region (PAR)" in the revised manuscript.

disp-quote.p: (13) Figure 1A: Please add the localization of pre-RNA (and other nucleolar components) in the mouse ES cells, etc., as a control. How the nucleolus in germ cells is similar or different from that in typical somatic cells is important.

body.p: We examined the localization of pre-rRNA in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF) as a representative somatic cell type (Figure S1A). Pre-rRNA showed a similar nucleolar localization pattern in MEFs and spermatogonia (SPG), indicating that the general organization of pre-rRNA within the nucleolus is comparable between these two cell types.

disp-quote.p: (14) Line 83, in situ: Should be italicized.

body.p: We have corrected all instances of "in situ" to italicized format (in situ) throughout the manuscript.

disp-quote.p: (15) Figure 1A and text: Please explain what Scp3 is and why the authors used this.

body.p: Synaptonemal complex protein 3 (SYCP3) is a major structural component of the lateral elements of the synaptonemal complex, a proteinaceous structure formed between homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase I. SYCP3 localizes along meiotic chromosome axes and is widely used as a marker to visualize chromosome organization and distinguish different substages of meiotic prophase I based on characteristic patterns of chromosome synapsis (PMID: 42059593). Therefore, we used SYCP3 staining to visualize meiotic chromosome axes and to identify the developmental stage of spermatocytes. We have now added a clear description of SYCP3 and the rationale for its use in the revised manuscript (Lines 54-56).

disp-quote.p: (16) Figure 1A and others, dispersion ratio: Please explain what the ratio is in the text and/or the legend.

body.p: The dispersion ratio is defined as the area of pre-rRNA signal divided by the total nuclear area (delineated by DAPI staining). This ratio reflects the degree of spatial dispersion of pre-rRNA within the nucleus: a higher ratio indicates a more diffuse distribution, whereas a lower ratio indicates a more concentrated localization. The dispersion ratio of NPM1 was calculated using the same method as that for pre-rRNA. We have now added a detailed explanation of this definition to the legend of Figure 1A.

disp-quote.p: (17) Figure S1A, top panels: A small portion of the signal of POLR1E (yellow) is out of the nucleus (white circle) and overlaps with c-Kit. What does this mean? Need to clarify.

body.p: The appearance of this small portion of POLR1E signal was most likely due to non-specific staining or an imaging artifact, as it was not reproducibly observed in other cells or independent experimental replicates. To avoid potential misinterpretation, we have replaced the original image with a new representative panel from the same experimental condition in the revised Figure S1A.

disp-quote.p: (18) Line 93. GC: Should be "NPM1", since this is the result.

body.p: We have corrected “GC” to “NPM1” in the corresponding sentence in the revised manuscript.

disp-quote.p: (19) Line 98-, Figure 1C: Please explain how the EU is incorporated into cells and what the "transient" means here in the legend.

body.p: 5-EU (5-ethynyl uridine) is a cell-permeable uridine analog that is incorporated into newly synthesized RNA during active transcription (PMID: 40701178; PMID: 37683610; PMID: 29431736). In our experiment, we added 5-EU to the culture medium at a concentration of 1 mM for 2 hours to transiently label newly synthesized RNA. The term "transient" refers to the short pulse-labeling period (2 hours), which allows us to capture a snapshot of active transcription at the time of labeling, rather than steady-state RNA accumulation.

disp-quote.p: (20) Line 110, coalesce: Without live imaging, it is very hard to show that NPM1 (or pre-rRNA) bodies coalesce. The authors need to soften the wording here.

body.p: We have replaced "coalesce" with " aggregate" (Line 116).

disp-quote.p: (21) Line 114, pre-rRNA and NPM1 are recruited and sequestered in the X-Y body; however, in Figure 2A, B. No evidence of the colocalization of the signals with a marker for X-Y bodies or X, Y chromosomes. How is it possible to quantify the signals without the reference marker, or how is the area of the X-Y body defined (right graphs, line 114-116)? It is essential to show the colocalization analysis in cytology.

body.p: In our study, the XY body territory was identified based on the following criteria: a. SYCP3 staining was used as the primary marker to delineate the axes of the X and Y chromosomes, which remain unsynapsed during pachynema and are embedded within the XY body. b. DAPI staining served as a secondary marker, as the XY body typically appears as a DAPI-dense region (heterochromatin-enriched) within the nucleus. Accordingly, the XY body area in our quantification (Figure 2A and 2B) was defined as the SYCP3-defined XY chromosome axis region plus the surrounding DAPI-dense chromatin territory, following the established criteria in references 20 and 38. We have now added this information to the corresponding Materials and methods section (Lines 496-501) to clarify our morphological analysis criteria.

disp-quote.p: (22) Line 115 gradual accumulation: This is true for Pre-rRNA, but not NPM1, which showed a sudden increase mid- to late-pachynema.

body.p: We have revised the wording from "gradual" to "dynamic" in the revised manuscript (Line 121).

disp-quote.p: (23) Figure S3, statistical analysis: What kind of statistics did the authors use here? It seems to be a simple quantification of the ratios.

body.p: In Figure S5 (originally presented in Figure S3), we quantified the dispersion ratio of pre-rRNA (or NPM1) across different meiotic stages. As defined in the figure legend, the dispersion ratio was calculated as the pre-rRNA (or NPM1) signal area divided by the total nuclear area (delineated by DAPI staining), which reflects the degree of spatial dispersion of the signal within the nucleus. The numbers indicated above the data points represent the mean value for each group, which facilitates direct comparison of the overall trend across different stages.

disp-quote.p: (24) Figure S4, line 126: Lamin is not a marker for the nuclear envelope. If the authors insist on an intact nuclear envelope (NE), please use the other NE markers.

body.p: We agree that Lamin is not a direct marker for the nuclear envelope (NE) per se. While the nuclear lamina is closely associated with the NE and provides structural support to the nucleus, it is not the envelope itself. Notably, Lamin B1 is widely used as a marker to assess nuclear envelope integrity (PMID: 15353547), because disruption of Lamin B1 localization is frequently accompanied by nuclear envelope abnormalities (PMID: 32954426; PMID: 23166514). Therefore, we consider it reasonable to use Lamin B1 staining as an indicator of NE integrity in our experimental context.

disp-quote.p: (25) Line 143-144, Figure S5A: How did the authors define the morphology of the X-Y body (what marker was used for the morphological analysis)?

body.p: Upon re-evaluation, we realized that SYCP3 staining, which we had originally used as a reference, lacks sufficient specificity to define the morphology of the XY body. Therefore, in the revised manuscript, we have deleted the morphological description in Page 7.

disp-quote.p: (26) Line 145, released: No experimental evidence for the release. Please rephrase here.

body.p: We have replaced "released" with "absent" in the revised manuscript (Line 151).

disp-quote.p: (27) Line 165, the treatment of spermatocytes with BMH-21: This is an in vitro experiment using isolated spermatocytes? As shown above, please mention the system precisely.

body.p: As the reviewer noted, the experiments were performed in vitro on isolated spermatocytes. Specifically, spermatocytes were isolated from mouse testes and treated with BMH-21 at 2.5 μM for 12 hours in culture medium, followed by fixation and immunofluorescence and RNA FISH analysis. We have now clarified the experimental system (Lines 172-173) and in the Methods section.

disp-quote.p: (28) Figure S7B. Please measure the weight of the testis.

body.p: We have now included the testis weight in the revised Figure S12B (corresponding to the original Figure S7B).

disp-quote.p: (29) Line 194, PNA: What is PNA? Please explain it to readers.

body.p: PNA (peanut agglutinin) is used as a marker for the acrosome of post-meiotic germ cells (round and elongated spermatids), and PNA-positive cells therefore represent post-meiotic spermatids. We have added this information in the revised manuscript (Lines 202-203).

disp-quote.p: (30) Figure 5A, PolII staining: The images shown in the figure are not convincing (cannot see any signals), which is not consistent with the quantification. Moreover, the graph shows the "relative" amount of PolII. How did the authors define 100% values here? Mean values are not 100% in the two graphs.

body.p: We have now corrected the y-axis to "Pol II-positive area within the XY body", which accurately reflects what was quantified. In the quantification graphs, the "Pol II-positive area within the XY body" refers to the percentage of the XY body territory that is occupied by Pol II signal. Specifically, the XY body region was defined as the region of interest based on SYCP3 staining and DAPI-dense chromatin. We have now added this definition to the Methods section (lines 496-501) to ensure clarity for readers.

disp-quote.p: (31) For the ATAC-seq in Figure 6, what happens to the accessibility of chromatin of autosomes (and sex chromosomes) in the BMH-21-treated cells relative to the mock control? In the text, the authors compared the accessibility of sex chromosomes relative to the autosomes only in the treated cells. It is critical to show the difference in the accessibility of autosomes in the treated and untreated cells.

body.p: The overall chromatin accessibility of autosomes remained unchanged upon BMH-21 treatment, whereas the accessibility of sex chromosomes was significantly increased under the same conditions (Figure 6B). Thus, the effect of BMH-21 on chromatin accessibility is preferentially associated with the sex chromosomes. The results have been included in Figure 6B and described in the Results section (Lines 239-245).
